Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Thornton, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Sarah Kline, Chief Medical Officer; Robert Lang, Chief Operating Officer; Jennifer Hale, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Patel, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: breakdown of revenue by service line, revenue per admission trends and drivers, impact of acuity mix changes on revenue, operating margin by segment, impact of recent acquisitions on financial performance, impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, and operating margin year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.

These achievements highlight our resilience in a dynamic healthcare services landscape, navigating CMS's shift toward value-based care, rising Medicare Advantage penetration, and the post-pandemic rebound in elective volumes. With that foundation, I’ll turn the call over to Michael Thornton to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $12.8 billion, an increase of 7.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $11.2 billion, representing 87.5% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain and labor optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $2.15 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Before we move on, let me dive deeper into these results, starting with the breakdown of our revenue by service line, which continues to reflect the resiliency and strategic evolution of our 180-hospital footprint across 25 states. For Q3, total net patient service revenues reached $12.8 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year, or 5.8% on a same-facility basis. This marks our 11th straight quarter of core growth, driven by a blend of volume expansion, modest pricing leverage from our commercial book-of-business refresh, and disciplined payer contract management.

Inpatient acute care services generated $5.1 billion, or 40% of total revenue, flat mix versus Q3 2023. Inpatient revenues grew 4.1% year-over-year, supported by 2.3% admissions growth to 285,000—our strongest Q3 since pre-COVID—and a 1.8% uptick in revenue per admission to $17,900. Patient days rose 3.2% to 1.65 million, with average length of stay stable at 5.8 days. Case mix index improved 1.5% to 1.92, fueled by higher-acuity ortho and neuro cases amid our robotic surgery program expansion—we're now at 95% platform penetration with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci systems across our acute facilities.

Regionally, Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida contributed 60% of this growth, benefiting from net migration and aging demographics; Texas alone saw 6% admissions growth on strong ortho volumes. Challenges persist in Rust Belt legacy markets, where Medicaid redeterminations post-unwinding shaved 50 basis points off growth. Strategically, we're leaning into this with our Value-Based Care initiative, where 35% of inpatient Medicare lives are now in bundled payments—reducing readmissions by 12% via our post-acute network partnerships.

Outpatient services came in at $4.7 billion, or 37% of total revenue, up 200 basis points year-over-year. This remains our fastest-growing segment, up 12.5% year-over-year and 10.2% same-facility, underscoring the industry-wide shift to lower-cost sites of service. Equivalent units grew 8.4%, with revenue per unit climbing 3.7% to $1,450, driven by imaging and procedural mix. Our 450+ ambulatory surgery centers and hospital outpatient departments were standout performers, capturing 15% more commercial elective cases like cataracts and colonoscopies amid payer pushback on site-neutral reimbursements under the OPPS final rule.

Notably, telehealth outpatient encounters surged 25% to 1.2 million, integrated via our Epic MyChart platform with AI-driven triage from Nuance's DAX Copilot, boosting no-show reductions by 18%. Regionally, urban clusters in the Southeast like Atlanta and Charlotte drove 70% of gains, while rural facilities lagged due to broadband gaps—we're addressing this with $50 million in federal BEAD funding for tele-outposts. Outlook: We expect outpatient to hit 40% mix by year-end, accelerated by our $2 billion ASC tuck-in M&A pipeline.

Emergency department and observation services totaled $1.6 billion, or 12% of total revenue, down 100 basis points year-over-year. ED revenues increased 3.8% on 4.2% volume growth to 2.1 million visits, with revenue per visit steady at $760. Observation stays—now 22% of ED encounters—grew 6%, capturing higher reimbursements under Medicare's 2-midnight rule clarifications. Trends reflect stabilizing acuity post-COVID surge, though boarding pressures eased 15% via our CarePort discharge lounge expansions.

High-growth Southwest EDs in Arizona and Nevada outperformed at +8%, tied to tourism rebound and uninsured-to-Medicaid conversions. We're mitigating reimbursement headwinds—Medicare ED pay down 2% on site-neutral policies—through upstream strategies like virtual ED with SOC Telemed, routing 30% of low-acuity cases digitally.

Ancillary and physician services rounded out at $1.4 billion, or 11% of total revenue, flat mix. This bucket, encompassing labs, imaging, pharmacy, and employed physician fees, rose 6.7% year-over-year. Key tailwinds: 9% growth in our 1,200-provider medical group via add-on acquisitions, and a 5% uptick in freestanding imaging volumes. Revenue cycle tech investments—including Change Healthcare's AI claims scrubbing post-Optum outage recovery—improved cash collections to 97% of billings. Midwest markets shone with lab outreach up 12% from hospital-at-home pilots.

Overall, our service line mix evolution—with outpatient gaining share at inpatient's expense—positions us for margin expansion in a 340B-constrained environment, where we've preserved $450 million in program benefits. Technical initiatives like our Oracle Health EHR migration, 85% complete, and predictive analytics for capacity management are yielding 2-3% efficiency gains. Looking ahead, we guide Q4 revenue growth to 7-8%, with outpatient leading at mid-teens. Risks include MA denial rates up 20% industry-wide and labor costs, but our 15% EBITDA margins—tops in the peer set alongside HCA—give us firepower for share repurchase and ASC buildouts.

Building on that revenue foundation, let's turn to revenue per admission trends and drivers. RPA came in at $17,900 for the quarter, up 6.2% year-over-year and 1.8% sequentially from Q2. This marks the strongest quarterly RPA growth we've seen since Q4 2021, outpacing the industry average of around 4-5% as reported by peers like HCA Healthcare and Community Health Systems.

RPA has now grown 18% cumulatively over the past three years, recovering from the pandemic-induced dip. This quarter, we lapped a tough comp from Q3 2023. Looking forward, we expect RPA to moderate to 4-5% growth in Q4 and into 2025, assuming no major payer reimbursement headwinds from the FY25 IPPS rule, which CMS finalized with a modest 2.9% update factor—better than proposed but below medical CPI inflation at 4.5%.

The primary driver was a 120-basis-point expansion in CMI to 1.92 from 1.78 a year ago. This reflects a shift toward higher-acuity admissions, with surgical volumes up 12% year-over-year, led by orthopedics—now 22% of total admissions—where RPA averaged $22,400 per case, a 9% increase driven by complex joint reconstructions and robotics-assisted procedures using Stryker's Mako system. Cath lab volumes grew 15%, boosted by PCI and TAVR, where RPA hit $28,500 amid favorable MS-DRG weights.

Payer mix contributed 200 basis points, with commercial managed care up 1.5 points to 48%, from narrow network contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Anthem in Sunbelt markets. This offset Medicare FFS decline to 32%, mitigated by value-based care pilots. Medicaid steady at 15%, though lags in Pennsylvania shaved 50 basis points.

Regionally, Southeast—Texas, Florida, Georgia, 55% of footprint—saw RPA surge 8.1% to $18,900, fueled by commercial mix at 52% and elective backlogs. Florida's no-fault auto reform accreted trauma RPA by 15-20%. Northeast markets grew only 3.2% to $16,000, dragged by Medicaid redeterminations and New York's caps; we're countering with CDI initiatives.

Technically, our CDI program with 3M 360 Encompass and AI NLP from Cerner generated $45 million additional revenue, up 25%, improving CC/MCC capture by 8%. Epic's Revenue Cycle module reduced denials to 4.2%, accelerating cash RPA to $17,200.

Strategically, service line optimization includes $150 million capex for six new ASCs in JV with United Surgical Partners, targeting high-RPA outpatient cases. Payer innovation like Humana MA risk-sharing delivered 7% uplift. Workforce stabilization improved nurse ratios to 1:4.2, reducing diversions.

Risks: pharma costs up 11%, MA clawbacks; hedged with derivatives.

Next, the impact of acuity mix changes on revenue was a key driver. System-wide CMI rose 3.2% year-over-year to 1.92, the fifth straight quarter of gains, outpacing CMS national average of 1.8%. This contributed 150 basis points to top-line growth, driving net patient revenue to $12.8 billion, up 7.2%, despite flat inpatient admissions at 285,000. Acuity-adjusted RPA climbed 4.8% to $17,900, revenue per patient day up 3.1% to $3,250—quality-over-quantity, like at HCA and UHS.

By service line, cardiovascular saw 12% MS-DRG weight increase from 15% rise in PCI/TAVR; structural heart program now in 18 of 52 hospitals with Medtronic/Edwards. Added $45 million. Neuroscience CMI up 8% on stroke/neuro-ICU via telestroke covering 85%. Oncology up 5% with CAR-T/Tempus AI, tempered by PA.

Dilution in ortho/general medicine from ASC shifts, site-neutral policies. LOS steady at 5.8 days, compressed 5% for high-acuity via ERAS.

Regionally, Southeast CMI +4.5% to 1.98 from retiree migration; Florida +10% Medicare ortho/cardiac added $28 million. Midwest -1.2% headwind reversed sequentially +2.1% with trauma center. West +2.8% from Medi-Cal, high denials.

Drivers: post-COVID backlog +22%, payer mix stable, Epic acuity analytics +7% capture, Cerner ML for CMI.

Strategically, bundled payments at five sites preserve upside. Guide full-year CMI 2.8-3.2%, $180-220 million incremental. Risks: outpatient shifts, IPPS cuts; counter with IR suites, proton centers. $120 million tailwind this quarter.

Shifting to operating margin by segment. Consolidated operating margin expanded 120 basis points year-over-year to 11.8%, driven by volume recovery, cost management, outpatient pivot.

Acute care hospitals, 62% revenues $7.9 billion, margin 7.2% up from 6.5% YoY. Adjusted admissions +5% to 285,000, ED traffic in Southeast. CMI 1.92, Medicare rates +2.8% vs. 4.5% inflation. Labor down to 48% via AI workforce platform like HCA/Kronos; contract labor 12%. Supplies 22%, Vizient bundles. Sunbelt +200 bps over Northeast. Target 8% via LOS to 4.4 days.

ASCs, 18% revenues $2.3 billion, margins 25.4% +310 bps YoY. Volumes +18% to 420,000, de novo in Dallas/Phoenix. Revenue/case +6% to $4,800, commercial 62%. Supplies 28% via surgeon committees like Tenet. Epic pre-op -12% no-shows. West lags, telehealth counter. Target 27% with Optum JVs.

Behavioral health, 12% $1.5 billion, 14.1% stable, down 50 bps YoY. Days +12% to 1.2 million, adolescent demand. Labor 52%, commercial 52%. Nexus EHR -0.8 LOS to 9.2. Midwest 16% vs. Northeast 12%. $50 million for IOP/Teladoc, target 15.5%.

Physician services, 8% $1.0 billion, 16.8% -120 bps on recruitment. Visits +10% to 1.8 million, wRVU 4,200. Centralized billing 98% claims.

Outpatient/physician now 45% EBITDAR. Labor +5.2%, supplies lag; $200 million tech. Target 12.5% Q4.

On recent acquisitions: $1.2 billion Southeast Surgical Partners (18 ASCs Florida/Georgia/Carolinas), $850 million Midwest Regional Hospitals (7 facilities, 1,200 beds Ohio/Indiana). Closed Q1/Q2, immediately accretive.

Pro forma $285 million revenue +22% standalone, 12 points of 18% consolidated growth. Same-store +6%. EBITDA $92 million at 32% margin, lifting consolidated $675 million +25%, 14 points from acquisitions. Ahead of underwriting: ASCs 45%, hospitals 18% post-integration.

Synergies $45 million YTD vs. $60 million target: $32 million cost (GPO Vizient -8% costs, Epic IT), $13 million revenue (cross-referrals +15% inpatient, denial -14%). 

Diversified footprint: Sunbelt 18% Florida revenues +28% volumes. Midwest offsets redeterminations, CMI +5%. Payer 52% gov, 38% MC, RPA +7% to $17,900.

BridgeTech $50 million: tele-nursing -12% RN, Cerner ALOS -0.4 to 4.2. ValueBridge ACO REACH 450,000 lives.

ROIC 14% > Tenet/UHS. FY25 +$120 million EBITDA, 200 bps expansion.

Value-based care contracts: 28% net revenue, up from 22%, > industry 13%. MSSP Track 3, ACO REACH, MA delegated, commercial capitation.

$42 million shared savings +35% YoY, 150 bps margin to 12.4% EBITDA. VBC cost -4.2%, readmits -22%, ED -15%.

Medicare VBC 65% $27 million, MSSP 92% quality, REACH 3.8% savings. Commercial $15 million, Texas MA MLR 82%.

Challenges: $75 million WC, BPCI -1.2% loss. Risk adjustment 95% 3M.

Epic Happy Together/Google API intervene 65% utilizers -18% admits. 8 Hubs 450 navigators, tele 2.1 visits/1k -12% cost.

Southeast 55% savings Humana MA. Midwest nascent, Aetna narrow network.

New contracts +75,000 lives Q4, ESRD/DaVita. $50 million fund. Target 35% revenue 2025, 200-300 bps accretion.

Finally, operating margin 12.8%, +70 bps QoQ from 12.1%, +260 bps YoY from 10.2%. High end vs. peers HCA/UHS.

YoY: revenue +8.2% outpaced expenses 450 bps. Volumes +4.8%, surgical +3.2%, CMI 1.92. Commercial 58%, MA 102% FFS. Labor +2.1% vs. 7.2%, Apex Flex -65% travel nurses, FTE +1.8%. Supplies -1.2% Vizient/ProcureHealth $28 million savings.

Southeast +320 bps to 15.2%, Midwest +180 bps to 10.5%.

QoQ: revenue +3.1%, admits +2.3%, CMI +1.5%, ALOS 4.6. Labor +1.2%, $12 million insurance, A/R 48 days.

High Reliability Model: Epic Harmony $40 million gains, VBC 28% +90 bps, micro-hubs.

Q4 13.0-13.5%, +200 bps YoY. Risks site-neutral. 65% FCF returns.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Sarah Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Integrated Care Pathways program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform and remote patient monitoring programs.

Following that, Robert Lang will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Robert Lang:
Thank you, Dr. Kline. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including centralized supply chain optimization and digital workforce scheduling, which have resulted in significant cost savings and improved patient flow.

Next, Jennifer Hale will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Jennifer Hale:
Thank you, Robert. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets and enhance our service offerings.

After that, David Patel will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

David Patel:
Thank you, Jennifer. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

David Patel:
Good morning, Sarah. Thankfully, we experienced no material impact from recent industry-wide cybersecurity threats on our operations or patient data. Our multi-layered defense strategy, including zero-trust architecture, continuous threat monitoring via our Splunk SIEM platform, and regular penetration testing by third-party experts like Mandiant, held firm. We've invested over $100 million in the past year to segment our Epic EHR environment, encrypt all PHI at rest and in transit, and deploy AI-driven anomaly detection from Darktrace. Post any alerts, our incident response time averaged under 30 minutes, with full recovery protocols tested quarterly. Patient trust remains high, with no breaches reported, and we're 100% compliant with HIPAA and HITRUST. This positions us ahead of peers, as evidenced by our top-quartile scores in the HIMSS Cybersecurity Survey. Happy to provide more details offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Sarah Kline:
Thanks for the question, Mike. We're aggressively scaling telehealth and RPM to meet growing demand and support value-based care. In Q3, we hit 1.2 million telehealth encounters, up 25%, and plan to double RPM enrollment to 100,000 high-risk patients by year-end, focusing on CHF, COPD, and post-acute ortho. Key expansions include integrating Nuance DAX Copilot for ambient documentation across all 180 facilities, partnering with Medtronic for RPM wearables in cardiac cohorts, and launching hospital-at-home programs in 50 sites with Livongo-derived analytics. This should reduce readmissions another 10-15% while capturing $150 million in new reimbursement under CMS chronic care management codes. Regulatory tailwinds like parity laws in 20 states bolster this. Early ROI shows 20% lower total cost of care, aligning with our CMO-led digital health roadmap.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Jennifer Hale:
Hi Emily, great question. Our partnerships are central to growth, with recent JVs like the six new ASCs with United Surgical Partners and Optum adding high-margin outpatient capacity, expected to contribute $200 million annualized revenue at 30% margins. We're deepening ties with pharma like Tempus AI for oncology precision medicine, unlocking bundled reimbursements, and payers like Humana for MA delegated risk on 75,000 lives. Post-acute alliances with Kindred at Home have cut readmits 12%, feeding VBC savings. Impact: these should drive 10% organic growth in 2025, diversify payer mix, and enhance service lines like structural heart with Edwards Lifesciences. ROIC targets 15%+, mirroring Tenet's playbook, while mitigating site-neutral risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Michael, can you elaborate on the margin outlook given labor and supply pressures?

Michael Thornton:
Sure, David. Q4 margins at 13.0-13.5% reflect continued leverage: labor growth moderating to 3%, supplies stable via Vizient, and VBC upside. We've de-risked with regional staffing academies and micro-hubs. Confident in 14% long-term.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
